questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

The chef had prepared all the dishes before the guests arrived.
options_en: All the dishes were prepared by the chef before the guests arrived.
All the dishes have been prepared by the chef before the guests arrived.
All the dishes had been prepared by the chef before the guests arrived.
All the dishes are prepared by the chef before the guests arrived.
questions.solution_en:
The subject of the Active Voice ("The chef") is changed into the object of the Passive Voice ("by the chef"). Also, the object of the Active Voice ("all the dishes") is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

The usage of a "to be" form ['been'] of verb is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

The Active voice in this question is in Past Perfect. Thus, the Passive voice will also be in Past Perfect.

The format of Active voice is: Subject + had + V3 + Object.

Thus, in Passive voice, the format will be: Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + had + been + V3 + by + Subject of the active voice (Objective case).

For example:

Arya had bought a new horse. (Active Voice)

A new horse had been bought by Arya. (Passive Voice)

The options except (c) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice:

· (a) uses simple past ("were prepared")

· (b) uses present perfect ("have been prepared")

· (d) uses simple present ("are prepared")

Therefore, the correct answer is (c): All the dishes had been prepared by the chef before the guests arrived.

Note: V1 -> Base form/simple form of verb, V2 -> Past form of verb (-ed form or irregular verb), V3 -> Past participle form of verb (-ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n), V4 -> Continuous form of verb / Present participle form of verb (-ing form), V5 -> Third person singular (V1+ -es or -s).

questions.q_en:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. Often referred to as the "rainforests of the sea," coral reefs are incredibly diverse underwater ecosystems built by colonies of tiny animals called coral polyps.

B. These vibrant structures provide essential habitats for approximately twenty-five percent of all marine species, making them one of the most biodiverse environments on the planet.

C. However, these vital ecosystems are currently facing unprecedented threats from climate change, pollution, and destructive fishing practices that cause widespread coral bleaching.

D. Each individual polyp secretes a calcium carbonate exoskeleton, and over thousands of years, these exoskeletons accumulate to form the massive structures we see today.
questions.solution_en:
The correct sequence is ADBC. Sentence A is the ideal opening sentence as it defines "coral reefs" and introduces the "coral polyps" that build them. Sentence D logically follows by explaining exactly how "Each individual polyp" (mentioned in A) contributes to building the "massive structures" of the reef. Sentence B then describes the immense ecological importance of "These vibrant structures" (the reefs from A and D), highlighting their role in supporting marine life. Finally, sentence C introduces a contrasting point with the word "However," shifting the focus to the "unprecedented threats" that "these vital ecosystems" are facing, which serves as a poignant conclusion.

Hence, option (b) is the answer.

questions.q_en:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. During this critical stage, the beans undergo the Maillard reaction and caramelization, which together create the complex aromas and flavours that we cherish in our cup.

B. After this process, the roasted beans are cooled down rapidly to halt the chemical reactions and lock in the desired flavour profile before they are packaged.

C. The roaster must meticulously control the temperature and timing, as even a few seconds can dramatically alter the final taste from bright and acidic to dark and bitter.

D. The art of coffee roasting is a transformative process where green, raw coffee beans are subjected to intense heat to unlock their intrinsic aromatic potential.
questions.solution_en:
The correct sequence is DCAB. Sentence D provides a general introduction to the "art of coffee roasting," explaining its fundamental purpose, making it the best starting point. Sentence C logically follows by detailing the precision required by the "roaster" during this process, emphasizing the importance of temperature and timing. Sentence A then delves into the specific chemical changes that occur "During this critical stage" (the roasting process from D and C), mentioning the Maillard reaction. Finally, sentence B describes the next step in the sequence, using the phrase "After this process" to logically signal the cooling stage that follows roasting.

Hence, option (c) is the answer.

questions.q_en:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

She dare (A)/ not to cheat (B)/ anyone again (C)/ in her life (D).
questions.solution_en:
If need/ dare is used in a negative sentence, 'not' should be followed by a 'bare infinitive'. It means we should use only 1st form of verb and not 'to +1st form of verb.' In the given sentence 'to' will be omitted.

So, the correct sentence is - 'She dare not cheat anyone again in her life'.

Hence, option (b) is the correct choice.

Note: Infinitive: The infinitive is the base form of a verb, often preceded by to.

Consider the sentences given below:

To err is human. [like a noun, the infinitive 'to err' is the subject of the verb 'is']

My father likes to cook. [like a noun, the infinitive 'to cook' is the object of the verb 'likes']

To vote in elections is our right. [the infinitive 'to vote', like a noun, is the subject of the verb 'is', but, like a verb, it also takes an object (elections)]

Radha went to the lake to fetch water. [the infinitive 'to fetch', like a noun, is the object of the verb 'went', but, like a verb, it also takes an object (water)]

The above sentences illustrate various ways in which infinitives are used. It can both act as a noun and a verb.

The company mainly

P. single-borrower corporate segment,

Q. which is riskier than the retail segment

R. operates in the large
questions.solution_en:

The final sentence is: The company mainly operates in the large single-borrower corporate segment, which is riskier than the retail segment.

Hence, (c) is correct.

questions.q_en:
Correct the following sentence.

One of the member of his family died due to a heart attack.
options_en: One of member from his family died of a heart attack.
One of the members of his family died due to a heart attack.
One of the members of him family died due to a heart attack.
One of the member of him family died due to a heart attack.
questions.solution_en:
The phrase 'one of the' is used to describe something/someone from the same group and it is always followed by a plural noun. So, the singular noun 'member' should be replaced by the plural noun 'members' in the given sentence. This is why the given sentence and options (a) and (d) are incorrect.

Option (c): 'his' instead of 'him' would be appropriate to refer to the family.

Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement'.

As we've been neighbours, I have known Mrs. Shashi Singh since more than 16 years.
questions.solution_en:
The preposition 'since' is used to refer to the point of time when an action began in the past and is still continuing. Here, '16 years' is a period of time. In such cases, the preposition 'for' should be used. For example:

We have been married since 1996.

I was waiting for an hour.

According to this, option (d) is the correct choice.

Note:

A Preposition is a word placed before a noun or a pronoun or a noun equivalent (pronoun, adverb, gerund, infinitive, adverbial clause, or any clause that can be used as the object of the preposition) and shows a relationship in space or time or a logical relationship between two or more people, places, or things in a sentence.

Examples

I. The teacher scolded the child for being late.

II. We're going to a party.

· The words in bold are called prepositions because they normally take a position before (pre) a noun/pronoun or a noun equivalent (pronoun, adverb, gerund, infinitive, adverbial clause, or any clause that can be used as the object of the preposition.

· The noun/pronoun which is used with a preposition is called its Object.

questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

We _________ conform to your demands.
questions.solution_en:
The blank requires an auxiliary verb phrase that supports the action 'conform' with respect to the noun 'demands'. 'Does/is/was not' correspond to a singular subject, but 'we' is a plural pronoun, so they will be negated. Moreover, 'conform' is in the base form of the verb (V1), so options c) and d) cannot be used and are thus negated. 'Do not' [plural verb] is the most appropriate form of the verb that supports the verb 'conform' as required in the sentence.

Hence, the correct answer is option (b).

The correct sentence is: We do not conform to your demands.

Note:

Auxiliary verb: A verb that gives grammatical information that is not given by the main verb of a sentence. It supports the main verb. Auxiliary verbs help to form the various tenses, moods, and voices of other verbs. The principal ones are be, do, and have. Example: She will sing a song tomorrow. Here, 'will' is the auxiliary verb that supports the main verb 'sing'.

V1 -> Base form/simple form of verb, V2 -> Past form of verb (-ed form or irregular verb), V3 -> Past participle form of verb (-ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n), V4 -> Continuous form of verb / Present participle form of verb (-ing form), V5 -> Third person singular (V1+ -es or -s).

Verb phrase: A verb phrase is the verbal part of a clause. A verb phrase has an ordinary verb (come, thought, left, climbing) and may also have an auxiliary verb (had, was, will) Example: She had already thought about the idea before. Here 'thought' is the main verb, 'had' the auxiliary verb and the highlighted part, the verb phrase.

Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

The removal of the preposition 'by' is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Passive to Active.

In Active voice (look at the options), it should be an interrogative sentence. The answer to this question will be either "yes" or "no".

These types of sentences usually begin with a helping verb like "Did".

In Passive voice, the format is: Was/Were + Subject (Objective case) + V3 + by + Object (Subjective case)?

Therefore, the format of the sentence which begins with "Did" in Active voice is: Did + Subject + V1 + Object?

For example:

Were you beaten by him? (Passive)

Did he beat you? (Active)

The options except (b) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Active Voice.

Thus, the correct answer is: (b) Did the country take up arms?

questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

I told Pooja that she could have use my car to get around while she is in my hometown.
options_en: that she could have use my car to get around with
that she can use my car to get around
that she could have use my car to get away
that she can use my car to get away with
questions.solution_en:
The usage of the word 'use' is incorrect in the underlined part. Either the third form of a verb should be used after the helping verb 'have', or the word 'have' should be removed from the sentence so that the first form of the verb fits appropriately after the modal verb 'could/can' in the sentence. So, options (a) and (c) are incorrect as they do not rectify this error.

Option (d) is incorrect as 'to get away with' means 'to escape'. It does not make the sentence coherent as one cannot escape a place and yet stay in the speaker's hometown.

Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

Note: Modal verb: A verb used with another verb to express an idea such as the possibility that is not expressed by the main verb. The modal verbs in English are "can," "could," "may," "might," "must," "ought," "shall," "should," "will," and "would." They do not change their form (spelling) and they have no infinitive or participle (past/present). Example: I can speak Spanish. questions.q_en:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains a grammatical error.

The wedding gown / looked decently / despite being / studded with jewels.
questions.solution_en:
When verbs of perception including look, taste, smell, feel and sound are used to express sensation or appearance, they are followed by adjectives, not adverbs. This means that 'looked' should be followed by 'decent' and not 'decently'.

The correct sentence is: The wedding gown looked decent despite being studded with jewels.

So, the part in option (c) has an error.

Hence, option (c) is the answer.

questions.q_en:
In the following question, one part of the sentence has an error. Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error and choose the option accordingly.

You have to try more hardly to gain subscribers for your magazines.
questions.solution_en:
'Hardly' is an adverb, and is used to suggest that something is unlikely to be or certainly not the case. The sentence talks about the effort put by them to gain subscribers. So, the adverb 'hardly' is grammatically incorrect, and it should be replaced with the adjective 'hard' to rectify the sentence. Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

The correct sentence is: You have to try more hard to gain subscribers for your magazines.

Or the sentence can modify as "You have to try harder to gain subscribers for your magazines."

Note:

· The Positive Degree of an Adjective is the Adjective in its simple form. It is used to denote the mere existence of some quality of what we speak about. It is used when no comparison is made.

· The Comparative degree of an adjective denotes a higher degree of the quality than the positive and is used when two things are compared.

· The Superlative degree indicates the highest degree of the quality and is used when more than two things (or sets of things) are compared.

questions.q_en:

questions.solution_en:

• (2) Bossy husbands → Incorrect, as the wife is usually the bossy one in this context.

• (4) Dominating husbands → Incorrect, as a "henpecked husband" is submissive, not dominant.

questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the word given in brackets to fill in the blank.

During the press conference, the CEO was forced to ________(repudiate) the false allegations made against his company by a rival firm.
questions.solution_en:
The sentence requires a synonym for "repudiate," which means to refuse to accept or be associated with; to deny the truth or validity of something.

d) renounce - means to formally declare one's abandonment of a claim, right, or possession; to reject and stop using or consuming. This is a strong synonym for "repudiate."

a) repeat - means to say again something one has already said. This is not the same as rejecting.

b) reconsider - means to consider something again, especially for a possible change of decision. This does not mean to reject.

c) accept - means to consent to receive a thing offered. This is an antonym of repudiate.

The complete sentence is: During the press conference, the CEO was forced to renounce the false allegations made against his company by a rival firm.

Hence, the most appropriate synonym is option (d).

questions.solution_en:

- Imminent: almost certain to happen very soon.

questions.q_en: Identify the sentence written in the active voice.
options_en: They won the series last year.
The series had been won by them last year.
The series would be won by them last year.
Last year, the series won by them.
questions.solution_en:
The absence of the helping verb and the preposition 'by' is necessary when the voice of the sentence is Active.

One of the formats of Active Voice is: Subject + V2 + Object.

The options except (a) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Active Voice. Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

He said, "I shall need a copy of the documents."
options_en: He said that he would need a copy of the documents.
He said that he is going to need a copy of the document.
He said that he will need a copy of the documents.
He said that he shall need a copy of the document.
questions.solution_en:
The sentence in the Direct Speech is in Future Simple Tense. Therefore, the sentence in the Indirect Speech should be in Present Conditional Tense.

Future Simple (Subject + will/shall + V1 + object) should be converted into Present Conditional (Subject + would/should + V1 +object).

For example:

He said, "I will be in Kolkata on Friday." (Direct Speech)

He said that he would be in Kolkata on Friday. (Indirect Speech)

The following thing in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

Shall-Would

Among the options, the sentence that follows the rules of Indirect Speech is "He said that he would need a copy of the documents."

Hence, the correct answer is option (a).
